question.prompt:
It is possible to choose \(x\gt\dfrac23\) in such a way that the value of

\[ \log_{10}(x^2+3)-2\log_{10}x \]

is:

solutions.explanation:
Combining the logarithms reveals how the expression changes when \(x\) grows. Since \(x>\frac23>0\), all logarithms are defined, and the expression is
\[
F(x)=\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{x^2+3}{x^2}\right)
=\log_{10}\!\left(1+\frac3{x^2}\right).
\]
The argument is greater than \(1\). Also, \(x^2>\frac49\), so
\[
0<F(x)<\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{31}{4}\right)<1.
\]
This excludes negative values, zero, one, and arbitrarily large values.

Now let \(t>0\) be any specified positive number. Because \(10^t-1>0\), we may choose
\[
x>\max\left\{\frac23,\sqrt{\frac3{10^t-1}}\right\}.
\]
Then \(1+3/x^2<10^t\). The base-10 logarithm is increasing, so
\[
0<F(x)<\log_{10}(10^t)=t.
\]
Thus the expression can be made smaller than any specified positive number, choice D.
solutions.title: Combine the logarithms and choose x
